newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Saudi Corral group to expand investment in Morocco.
newsitem.headline: Saudi Corral group to expand investment in Morocco.

text.p: Swedish-based Saudi Corral group, which recently bought Morocco's two oil refineries, has set up a local firm to expand its oil investments, a spokesman for Corral said on Thursday.

"We have just set up a new firm in Morocco's financial centre, Casablanca, called Corral Morocco Holding as part of our strategy to expand our investments in the country's oil sector," a spokesman for Corral Petroleum Holding AB told Reuters.
The spokesman, who declined to be named, gave no details of the new firm's capital.

Members of Corral management visited the Moroccan capital Rabat earlier this week where "they finalised the $419 million (oil refineries) deal with the Moroccan privatisation ministry," the spokesman said.
Morocco sold off state majority stakes in Samir and Societe Cherifienne des Petrolesfor a total of 3.9 billion dirhams ($419 million) to the Saudi group last month.
The group bought 67.7 percent of Samir, the main oil refinery, for 3.5 billion dirhams and 73.9 percent of SCP for 473 million dirhams, the privatisation ministry said.
The group agreed to invest a further 3.8 billion dirhams in the oil sector and preserve domestic employment over a period of five years, the ministry said.
"Considering our privileged position on the domestic market, we plan to extend our business to Morocco's oil distribution network," the Corral spokesman said.
Preliminary talks were held in Casablanca with some local filling station managers on "possibilities for joint-venture projects," he said.
According to Corral, imports of crude oil, mainly from the United Arab Emirates and Iran, would remain unchanged "because they are based on costs and profitability."
Corral said its purchase of the refineries was motivated by "their monopoly of importing and refining crude oil in Morocco...Also for profit-making opportunities in the sector on the long term."
Morocco liberalised its oil sector two years ago but imports of refined products are heavily taxed to protect the local refining industry, a stockbroker said.

Located in a 200 hectares (500 acre) site in Mohammedia on the Atlantic coast, near Casablanca, the Societe Maroccaine de l'Industrie de Raffinage (Samir) has a capacity of 6.25 million tonnes per year or 80 percent of the country's needs for refined oil products.
The company, founded in 1959, has also a storage capacity of nearly 900,000 cu metres for crude oil and 870,000 cu metres for refined oil.

Corral group holds 100 percent in Swedish Preem Petroleum firm which has 550 distribution stations throughout Sweden. It has also two oil refineries in the country with a total capacity of 300,000 barrels per day.
